topic: Uniform and Non-uniform Mixtures, Solutions, and Suspensions
key_concepts: A mixture is a physical combination of two or more substances that retain their individual
Making a mixture does not form new matter
Mixtures can be homogeneous or uniform
Mixtures can be heterogeneous or non-uniform
Homogeneous mixtures have uniform composition and one visible phase
Heterogeneous mixtures have visibly different and unevenly distributed components
Vinegar, sugar solutions, alloys, and air are examples of homogeneous mixtures
Beach sand, fruit salad, salad dressing, and clouds are examples of heterogeneous mixtures
Solutions are homogeneous mixtures formed when a solute dissolves in a solvent
A solute is the substance that is dissolved and a solvent is the substance that dissolves
Dissolving breaks a substance into molecules that mix with another substance's molecules
